chapters.title: Chapter 68 · One good at being a warrior
chapters.intro: Lists what the best commanders, fighters, victors and employers of people look like: not warlike, not angry, not clashing head-on, humble toward others. This is the power of not competing, the way to use others' strength, and a match for heaven.

verses.en: One good at being a warrior is not martial; one good at fighting is not angry; one good at defeating enemies does not engage them; one good at using people places himself below them. This is called the virtue of not contending; this is called using the strength of others; this is called matching heaven, the utmost of antiquity.

cmp.note: 王弼本连写，通行断作「配天，古之极」（合乎天，是自古的最高准则），白话取这一种；也有学者认为「古」字是后来多出来的，应读「配天之极」。
cmp.en: Wang Bi's text runs pei tian gu zhi ji 配天古之极 together. It is usually split as "matching heaven, the utmost of antiquity"; some scholars think gu 古 (ancient) is a later intrusion, giving "the utmost of matching heaven".

chapters.title: Chapter 69 · Those who wage war have a saying
chapters.intro: Quotes a military saying: rather defend than attack, rather fall back a foot than advance an inch. The worst disaster is taking the enemy lightly, which nearly costs the speaker his treasures, and when two armies clash, the side that grieves will win.

verses.en: Those who wage war have a saying: "I dare not be the host but would rather be the guest; I dare not advance an inch but would rather retreat a foot." This is called marching without a march, raising arms without arms, confronting without an enemy, holding without weapons.
No disaster is greater than taking the enemy lightly; taking the enemy lightly nearly costs me my treasures. Therefore, when opposing armies meet, the side that grieves will win.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 · My words are very easy to understand
chapters.intro: The speaker says his words are easy to understand and easy to practice, yet no one does either, because people miss the principle behind them. Few understand him, so the sage is like someone in rough clothes with jade hidden inside.

verses.en: My words are very easy to understand and very easy to practice. Yet no one under heaven can understand them, and no one can practice them.
Words have an ancestor; deeds have a master. It is only because people do not understand this that they do not understand me. Those who understand me are few; those who follow me are precious.
Therefore the sage wears coarse cloth and carries jade in his bosom.

chapters.title: Chapter 71 · To know that one does not know
chapters.intro: Knowing that you don't know is best; thinking you know when you don't is a sickness. The sage is free of this sickness because he recognizes it as a sickness.

verses.en: To know that one does not know is best; not to know yet think one knows is a sickness.

cmp.note: 白话取通行读法「知道自己不知道，最好」；另一种读法是「知道了却不自以为知道，最好」。
cmp.en: Zhi bu zhi 知不知 is usually read as "to know that one does not know"; another reading is "to know but not to think one knows".

verses.en: Only by treating the sickness as sickness is one free of sickness. The sage is free of sickness because he treats the sickness as sickness; therefore he is free of sickness.

chapters.title: Chapter 72 · When the people do not fear authority
chapters.intro: Rulers should not squeeze people's homes and livelihoods; once people stop fearing authority, worse trouble comes. The sage knows himself without showing off and values himself without putting himself above others.

verses.en: When the people do not fear authority, a greater dread arrives.
Do not cramp the places where they dwell; do not crush the means by which they live. Only by not crushing them will one not be rejected.

cmp.note: 两个「厌」字意思不同：前一个通「压」（压迫），后一个是「厌弃」。白话按这个分开译。王弼本的「狎」，通行读作「狭」（逼迫）。
cmp.en: The two yan 厌 differ: the first means "to press down, oppress", the second "to be weary of, reject". Xia 狎 in Wang Bi's text is usually read as xia 狭 (to cramp).

verses.en: Therefore the sage knows himself but does not display himself, loves himself but does not exalt himself; thus he discards that and takes this.

chapters.title: Chapter 73 · Courage in daring
chapters.intro: Courage that dares gets one killed; courage that holds back keeps one alive, and no one can say why heaven dislikes the first. Heaven's way wins without fighting, answers without speaking and plans without hurry; its net is wide-meshed yet misses nothing.

verses.en: Courage in daring leads to death; courage in not daring leads to life. Of these two, one benefits and one harms. What heaven hates, who knows the reason? Therefore even the sage finds it difficult.

The Way of heaven does not contend yet is good at winning, does not speak yet is good at responding, does not summon yet things come of themselves, is unhurried yet good at planning. Heaven's net is vast; its mesh is wide, yet nothing is lost.

chapters.title: Chapter 74 · The people do not fear death
chapters.intro: If people no longer fear death, threatening them with it is pointless. Killing belongs to the one whose task it is; a ruler who kills in its place is like an amateur doing a master carpenter's cutting, and rarely escapes cutting his own hand.

verses.en: If the people do not fear death, why threaten them with death? If the people were made always to fear death, and I could seize and kill those who do wicked things, who would dare?

There is always the executioner who does the killing. To kill in place of the executioner is called hewing in place of the master carpenter. Of those who hew in place of the master carpenter, few do not injure their own hands.

chapters.title: Chapter 75 · The people starve
chapters.intro: People go hungry, become hard to govern and stop fearing death, all because of those above them: heavy taxes, constant interference and lavish living. One who does not make living well his goal is wiser than one who prizes life too much.

verses.en: The people starve because those above them eat too much in taxes; that is why they starve. The people are hard to govern because those above them are always acting; that is why they are hard to govern. The people make light of death because those above them seek life too richly; that is why they make light of death.

cmp.note: 王弼本有「上」字，白话按「在上面的人求生太过」译；有些本子没有「上」字，读成百姓自己求生太过。
cmp.en: Wang Bi's text has shang 上 (those above), so the excess belongs to the rulers; some texts lack it, making it the people's own eagerness for life.

verses.en: Only one who does not make living his aim is wiser than one who prizes life.

chapters.title: Chapter 76 · When people are alive
chapters.intro: People and plants are soft and supple when alive and stiff and dry when dead. So hardness goes with death and softness with life: an army that relies on force does not win, and a hard tree gets cut down.

verses.en: When people are alive they are soft and weak; when dead they are hard and stiff. When the myriad things, grasses and trees are alive they are soft and tender; when dead they are dry and withered.

Therefore the hard and stiff are companions of death; the soft and weak are companions of life. Thus when an army is strong it does not win; when a tree is strong it meets the axe. The strong and great dwell below; the soft and weak dwell above.

cmp.note: 王弼本作「兵」，通行理解为「遭到兵器（刀斧）砍伐」，白话取这一种；《列子》引作「折」，另有本子作「共」。
cmp.en: Wang Bi's text has bing 兵 (weapon), read as "meets the blade"; the Liezi quotes it as zhe 折 (snaps), and some texts have gong 共.

chapters.title: Chapter 77 · The Way of heaven
chapters.intro: Heaven's way is like drawing a bow: it lowers what is high, raises what is low, takes from excess and gives to lack. People do the opposite, taking from those who lack to serve those who have plenty. Only someone with the Way gives his surplus to the world.

verses.en: Is not the Way of heaven like the stretching of a bow? What is high is pressed down, what is low is raised up; what has excess is reduced, what is lacking is supplemented.

The Way of heaven reduces what has excess and supplements what is lacking. The way of people is not so: it reduces what is lacking to offer to what has excess. Who can take his excess and offer it to the world? Only one who has the Way.
Therefore the sage acts but does not rely on it, accomplishes his work but does not dwell in it; he does not wish to display his worth.

chapters.title: Chapter 78 · Nothing under heaven is softer
chapters.intro: Water is the softest thing, yet nothing beats it at wearing down the hard. Everyone knows the soft defeats the hard, but no one acts on it. The sage says only one who takes on a country's shame and misfortune is fit to rule it. True words sound backwards.

verses.en: Nothing under heaven is softer and weaker than water, yet in attacking the hard and strong nothing can surpass it, for nothing can take its place.

cmp.note: 「易」通行读作「代替」，白话取这一种；也有人读作「改变」：没有什么能改变水（柔弱的本性）。
cmp.en: Yi 易 is usually read as "replace"; it can also mean "change": nothing can alter water.

verses.en: That the weak overcomes the strong and the soft overcomes the hard, no one under heaven does not know, yet no one can practice it.

Therefore the sage says: "One who takes on the disgrace of the state is called lord of the altars of soil and grain; one who takes on the misfortunes of the state is king of all under heaven." Straight words seem to be their opposite.

chapters.title: Chapter 79 · Settling a great resentment
chapters.intro: Settling a deep grudge always leaves some bitterness, so the sage holds the creditor's half of the contract but does not demand payment. People of virtue are lenient, those without it are harsh. Heaven has no favorites and always sides with the good.

verses.en: When a great resentment is settled, some resentment is sure to remain; how can this be counted as good?
Therefore the sage holds the left half of the tally but makes no demands on others. One with virtue keeps the tally; one without virtue keeps the levy.
The Way of heaven has no favorites; it is always with the good.

chapters.title: Chapter 80 · A small state with few people
chapters.intro: Pictures an ideal small country with few people. Labor-saving tools, boats, carts and weapons go unused, and people stay put. They enjoy their own food, clothes, homes and customs; the next country is within sight and earshot, yet they never visit it all their lives.

verses.en: A small state with few people: let there be implements worth ten or a hundred, yet let them not be used; let the people take death seriously and not move far away. Though there are boats and carriages, there is no occasion to ride them; though there are armor and weapons, there is no occasion to array them.

cmp.note: 通行理解为「能顶十个、百个人的器具」，白话取这一种；河上公本作「什伯人之器」，有人解作军中十人、百人一组用的兵器。
cmp.en: Shi bo zhi qi 什伯之器 is usually read as "implements worth ten or a hundred people"; another reading takes shi bo as army units of ten and a hundred, making these weapons.

verses.en: Let people return to knotting cords and using them; let them find their food sweet, their clothes fine, their dwellings peaceful, their customs joyful. Neighboring states are within sight of one another, the sounds of roosters and dogs are heard from one to the other, yet the people grow old and die without going back and forth.

chapters.title: Chapter 81 · True words are not beautiful
chapters.intro: The closing chapter. True words are not pretty and pretty words are not true; good people do not argue, and those who truly know do not merely know a lot. The sage does not hoard: the more he gives, the more he has. Heaven benefits without harming; the sage acts without competing.

verses.en: True words are not beautiful; beautiful words are not true. The good do not argue; those who argue are not good. Those who know are not broadly learned; the broadly learned do not know.

The sage does not hoard. Having done all for others, he has more himself; having given all to others, he has still more himself. The Way of heaven benefits and does not harm; the Way of the sage acts and does not contend.
